title: Phloem: a sieve tube and its companion cells
caption: Sieve tube elements are living cells joined end to end, with sieve plates between them; they have few organelles and no nucleus. Each is served by a companion cell, which has a nucleus and many mitochondria and loads sucrose using ATP; plasmodesmata link the two.
alt: Two sieve tube elements stacked end to end with a perforated sieve plate between them, each with a companion cell beside it containing a nucleus and mitochondria, joined to it by narrow channels.
description: Sieve tube elements are living, with few organelles and no nucleus.
Sieve plates are perforated cross-walls that let sap pass.
Companion cells have a nucleus and many mitochondria: they supply ATP and load sucrose.
Plasmodesmata link each companion cell to its sieve tube element.
